positions.as_written: Address body mass alongside alignment, since it is the stronger modifiable factor.
Avoid reading a cross sectional association as a causal direction.
Assess the opposite compartment before correcting alignment, because the correction moves load onto it.
Offer weight reduction and gait modification as part of the mechanical plan rather than instead of it.

Take the patient's age, physiology, comorbidities, knee demand, psychological state and their own ideas, concerns and expectations into the decision, because the window in which correction is rational is narrow and the operation is large.
